rationale: The golden run fails SR3 with a golden_rejected failure class, but this is not an evaluator bug: the shipped decoder_netlist.v does not actually implement the documented Trojan symptom. Structural analysis shows bank2_we_comb is driven by an OR of sel2_we and a redundant minterm3-and-write_en tap (an alias gate feeding bank2), while bank3_we is independently driven by the legitimate sel3_we path which also fires at addr=011. Since bank0_we is only ever driven by minterm0 (addr=000), it can never assert at addr=011 regardless of write_en. Therefore the actual simulated asserted set at addr=011,we=1 is {bank2_we, bank3_we}, not {bank0_we, bank2_we} as the hidden ground truth, design_brief.md, and golden/trojan_report.json all claim. This is a genuine inconsistency in the case artifacts (netlist wiring vs. documented/expected ground truth), not a flaw in evaluate.py's SR3 check, which correctly cross-checks against simulated behavior per the evaluation contract. The evaluator behaves exactly as intended: it grades the submission's claims against exhaustively-simulated ground truth. Since the artifact (netlist) itself doesn't produce the documented behavior, the golden solution -- which correctly describes what SHOULD happen per the spec narrative -- is rejected because the actual wiring is wrong. This requires regenerating/fixing decoder_netlist.v (or fully revising the ground truth/golden to match actual simulated behavior) so that the documented SR2/SR3 semantics (bank0_we and bank2_we alias at addr=011) are what the netlist actually produces.
revision_instructions: The netlist artifact inputs/decoder_netlist.v does not produce the documented bridging behavior. Per the hidden ground truth and design_brief.md, address 011 with write_en=1 must cause exactly bank0_we and bank2_we to assert together (an aliasing/bridging Trojan). But as currently wired, bank0_we is driven solely by the addr==000 minterm and can never assert at addr=011; meanwhile bank3_we's legitimate decode also fires at addr=011, so the actual simulated asserted set is {bank2_we, bank3_we}, contradicting the documented ground truth. Regenerate the netlist so that: (1) the legitimate one-hot mapping for addresses 000-011 selects bank0..bank3 respectively as documented, (2) the hidden alias/bridging gate taps the addr==011 condition (ANDed with write_en) and ORs it into bank0_we's enable tree (not bank2's) so that at addr=011,write_en=1 both the legitimately-targeted bank (whichever the ground truth intends, e.g. bank0 or bank3 per a revised documented mapping) and bank2_we (the security-relevant bank) assert simultaneously, exactly matching {bank0_we, bank2_we}, (3) no other address produces more than one asserted write-enable. After fixing the wiring, regenerate golden/trojan_report.json to match the corrected simulated behavior, and re-run the differential harness (golden vs. naive baseline) to confirm golden_run exits 0 with all requirements passing and vulnerable_run correctly fails SR1/SR2/SR3/SR4/SR5. Also re-verify FR1-FR4 and the exhaustive one-hot invariant hold for all 7 non-triggering addresses via tb_exhaustive.v before resubmitting for validation.
